title: Graphspeak: of language and handshake
description: An experiment on decomposing language onto initially established graph-theory representation applied then onto some pre-selected transformations  (commonly used context/tool related transmutes) (t1,t2,t3) then upon some layers of decomposition finding out the shared context / what we label as a handshake; for the purpose of education / others

methods.name: Proposed three-layer graph sampling, conversion and decomposition scheme
methods.description: Outlines Layer 0-2 steps: sampling nodes with graph theory, converting via chosen permutative formats, then decomposing and comparing similarity.
methods.evidence: Sampling original intention and output using Graph Theory (math) - Converting it based on a staple table of known tools (limbs, etc) - Decomposing the Graph Theory nodes onto connected middle layers - Representing the handshake

methods.name: Three provisional 'transmute' rules for node composition (Tr1-Tr3)
methods.description: Defines three temporary notational norms for combining and decomposing nodes, illustrated with car-component examples.
methods.evidence: Engine. Wheel. Chasis = Car onto Engine –[snug-onto][snug-chasis]- Chasis - [snug-onto][snug-chasis] – Wheel = Car

methods.name: Planned pipeline of LLM querying with manual human confirmation
methods.description: Proposes data flows in which LLM labeling of objects and transmutes is followed by a manual confirmation layer before stashing.
methods.evidence: Sampling data > Pre-Process (labeling objects; et) -> Stash -> LLM Query (labeling) -> Manual Confirmation -> Stash

methods.name: Proposed graph-composition game as a test and application vehicle
methods.description: Describes a planned game in which players compose trees of 3-node graphs and apply preselected transmutation types.
methods.evidence: We also seek to make a game; On which seeks to picture itself this way “ Please Help this ## person , compose a Graph “ as an interactive way to both test & apply graphspeak

key_findings: Defines graphspeak as an experimental communication method whose medium is permutative graphs requiring a pre-handshake selection of sampling nodes.
Argues that such a language's success depends not on rigor but on empathy, framed as composing the recipient's capability with their context.
States planned objectives of testing deployment for kids, for cross-language generalizability, and for rigor.
key_findings_evidence: Graphspeak is an experimental method of communication Where the transmission medium is based on <permutative> Graphs By permutative, we mean that it requires a Pre-handshake; selection of sampling nodes
Being a successful medium, does not actually depend on their RIGOR But rather on their rating of <empathy>
Test its deployment for kids (results may depend more on how fun the game is; still! )
